_about: A division is laid once (release 2, the grand campaign; the design director's rulings of 13:43Z to 14:28Z, 25 November 2026; src/campaign/drawn.ts). The lines the player reads when a dated arrival names a division he already holds: it stays with his corps, no second one is raised, and sending it is his own order to give (her ruling 4 of 14:28Z: the row's line tells him the row names it). {names} the divisions, {place} where the arrival was due, {where} where his own stand, {was} the division another was to be formed out of. `stood`: the line of a lent force's end where its corps does not leave (it holds divisions that had no corps to go back to): {adj} the country's, {in} the campaign's theatre (" in the Balkans", or nothing), {names} the corps by the names they stand on under. `here`, `hereMany`: every division named stands at {place} already, so the place is said once. The words are the UI director's (16:48Z, 25 November 2026): one phrase in all, "No division is raised twice", and the plain promise of what he does about it. Her marks of 17:26Z: a place can be a region, so every line says "in"; `from` and `fromMany` are the stood war rows' lines (counting.json), a division or so many divisions the row was to draw from one of his corps: {army} that corps, {where} where it stands, {count} how many, in words, {formation} the row's own name. {at}: where his own stand, `ashore` (in {where}) or, for a corps on a passage, `afloat` (at sea, bound for {to}): the UI director's marks of 21:52Z (ui-director/drawn-afloat-UI-MARKS.md). `hereSea`, `hereSeaMany`: every division named is at sea bound for {place} already, so he has sent it. `manyPart`: some of them are bound for {place} already and some are not (the UI director's 21:59Z).
one: {names} is due in {place} this month, but you hold it already, {at}. No division is raised twice: it goes to {place} only if you send it.
many: {names} are due in {place} this month, but you hold them already, {at}. No division is raised twice: they go to {place} only if you send them.
here: {names} is due in {place} this month, and it is there already with your own forces. No division is raised twice.
hereMany: {names} are due in {place} this month, and they are there already with your own forces. No division is raised twice.
manyPart: {names} are due in {place} this month, but you hold them already, {at}. No division is raised twice: those not on their way there go to {place} only if you send them.
hereSea: {names} is due in {place} this month, and it is on its way there already with your own forces, at sea. No division is raised twice.
hereSeaMany: {names} are due in {place} this month, and they are on their way there already with your own forces, at sea. No division is raised twice.
conv: {names} was due to be formed in {place} this month out of your {was}, {at}. No division is raised twice: it is not formed, and your {was} stays as it is.
from: {names} was due in {place} this month, drawn from your {army} {at}. No division is raised twice: it is not formed, and your {army} keeps every division it has.
fromMany: {count} divisions were due in {place} this month to make up the {formation}, drawn from your {army} {at}. No division is raised twice: they are not formed, and your {army} keeps every division it has.
stood: {adj} formations lent to the campaign{in} are on loan no longer. With no corps to go back to, they stay where they stand, free for new orders: {names}.
